newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann sees 1997 telecoms profit flat.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann sees 1997 telecoms profit flat.

text.p: Germany's Mannesmann AG said on Wednesday that its plans to invest in its mobile phone business this year would keep its telecoms profits flat compared to last year.
"Because of investment in Arcor and other areas, there will be no increase in 1997," managing board member Klaus Esser told a news conference, referring to Mannesman's main telecoms unit.

Arcor, a joint venture with German state railways Deutsche Bahn AG, was expected to see a loss of 300 million marks this year. The company, which started up last August, lost 100 million marks in 1996.
Esser said that Mannesmann planned to invest nine billion marks in telecommunications over the next five years.
He added investment would go towards expanding Mannesmann's D2 mobile phone network and a planned venture with Generale des Eaux unit Cegetel in France, as well as to Arcor.
Last year, Mannesmann's telecoms operations earned a profit on ordinary activities of 947 million marks, accounting for nearly all of group profits of 1.01 billion marks.
